# John Company India companion — current implementation

## Scope
An unofficial local-save companion to the physical John Company Second Edition board. The 1710 campaign tracks eight regions, orders, towers, empires, Company Presidencies, unrest, loot-token availability, relevant laws, China office creation and the Elephant. The app owns the event stack; players retain Army inventories, writers, money, ships, votes and officeholders. No player identities are stored.

## Action interface
There are no manual board corrections. Map orders and region status are read-only. Deploy and Game actions calculate board changes and display physical instructions before confirmation. Confirming applies a complete validated action atomically, records it in history and saves it locally. Undo restores the previous app state; physical changes must be reversed at the table.

All choice fields appear as large buttons. Numeric fields use increase/decrease controls. Saved games provides naming, snapshots, imports and exports. Begin next turn advances the 1710 turn counter and resets rules limits derived from the recorded turn. Legacy campaign saves and prior correction-history entries remain readable.

## Deploy
Players choose an Army and a legal target, report committed forces, their final physical check outcome and officer losses. Rerolls are handled on the table. With no Company territory the Army can target only its own home region; expansion requires territory of its Presidency. Foreign home regions are excluded. Company targets require unrest or a closed order.

Defence shows every region in the defending empire and its tower contribution. Army-specific alliances are enforced. Success opens all target orders, removes unrest, handles control and released subjects, and redirects an outward-facing Elephant originating in the conquered region inward. The fixed regional loot bonus is included only while its token remains available. Values: Punjab £6, Delhi £8, Bengal £6, Bombay £4, Maratha £3 (user confirmed), Hyderabad £7, Mysore £5, Madras £5. Existing Company control retains its Presidency. Subsequent takeovers do not restore the bonus. Treasury Reform redirects loot to Company Balance.

## Administration
Without Governor General, Add unrest asks for Unsuccessful Administer or Successful Tax. The former adds one cube, or two with Zamindar Taxes. Report Tax is also a dedicated action: report every successful Tax, including the first. Its first report for each region and turn records the Tax without adding unrest; subsequent reports add one cube each. Choosing Tax in Add unrest uses this same counter. Tax cubes are not multiplied by Zamindar Taxes or Sepoy Recruitment. Payment remains on the physical board.

With Governor General, Add unrest accepts only Tax and prevents a repeated Tax placement in the same region during the same turn. Governor General check reports Success, Failure or Catastrophic failure plus the number of sixes. Each six adds one cube to every Company region; an unsuccessful check additionally adds one per region, or two with Zamindar Taxes. A successful Govern prevents further Govern checks that turn. Income and ship/regiment choices are performed on the table.

The separate Governor General box lists affected Company regions and offers Report Govern check & sixes and Governor General Tax. A General Tax always adds one unrest and each placement must use a different Company region that turn; it does not use the first-Tax exemption for individual Governors. Regional Add unrest is disabled under Governor General with a pointer to the company-wide controls. Regional Tax remains available for eligible placements. Tax counts and placement limits use the saved turn history, persist in snapshots/exports, reverse with Undo and reset for the next turn. Existing legacy additional-Tax records imply a prior first Tax; previously unrecorded first Taxes cannot be reconstructed.

## Actions from the region dossier

Selecting a region exposes Deploy here and Special Envoy, plus Report Tax and Add unrest for Company regions. The region context is locked in each dialog. Availability respects phase timing, game closure, relevant laws, ownership and the board state, with visible explanations beside disabled actions.

Deploy here opens army selection for the selected target. All three Armies are displayed as touch buttons; ineligible Armies are disabled with reasons for wrong home region, lack of an associated Company base bordering the target, catastrophe this turn, or no effect. Legal-target computation and these explanations share the same rules. An Indian region with no eligible Army disables Deploy here. A Company region with open orders and no unrest still allows inspection of the deployment dialog, but every Army and Continue are blocked where appropriate; the resolver also rejects a deployment with no effect. Selected-region deployment skips target selection and retains the existing live empire-strength breakdown and automatic loot calculation. Deploy is an ephemeral form: X or Cancel abandons all unconfirmed entries, and reopening any region starts fresh. Back preserves entries only while that dialog remains open.

Regional Special Envoy offers only eligible closed orders in that region outside Company control, and cannot create China through the regional shortcut. It is disabled if no such orders exist, Company Operation has ended, or Governor General has replaced Director of Trade. The global Special Envoy entry retains its China option when the office is eligible. The physical check outcome is reported before opening the chosen order. Sources: Deploy p.22, Special Envoy p.19, Governor Tax p.24 and Governor General p.26.

Unrest removal is automatic through successful Deploy, successful Company defence, inside-region Peace and Region Loss. Sepoy Recruitment doubles unrest’s attack contribution; it creates no cubes.

## Events
Normal events draw from the saved 20-tile digital stack, supplying the drawn front, modifier, front symbol and newly exposed back region automatically. Manual event resolution remains available as a test action that changes map state without consuming a digital tile or phase event. The event families implemented are Turmoil, Windfall, Shuffle, Leader, Peace, Crisis and Foreign Invasion.

Turmoil closes the geographically northernmost open order. Closures give writer/filled-token instructions. A wholly closed region Cascades along the 20 printed trade links. Each connected destination order is handled once per originating Cascade. An already closed destination falls back to the northernmost open order in its region; an entirely closed region Cascades. Each region can Cascade once per event, but can receive additional closure effects.

Peace on a border opens orders connected through that border and strengthens touching Indian regions. It does not remove unrest there. Peace inside a region opens all its orders and clears its unrest. Leader strengthens a sovereign region or resolves the indicated rebellion. Ordinary Indian invasion changes allegiance without closing orders or consuming loot. Successful rebellion closes the rebelling region’s orders. Capital conquest releases its former subjects. Empire flags are limited to three sets; capital flag allocation persists even if its last subject rebels.

Company attacks collect the available strength exhausted on the table. Defence is an exhaustion comparison, not a Deploy roll. Resolve the primary attack before additional unrest rebellions in Presidency order Bombay, Madras, Bengal; when several additional regions share a Presidency, players choose their order. Each subsequent attack uses the current state. Pieces do not refresh. Region Loss reports Commander consequences, officer rout, Governor removal where relevant, dome restoration, orders, spent loot and cumulative Standing loss for the physical turn. Vacant-office acting rules are stated in the dialog.

Each lost Company region requires a separate Officer Rout result page before subsequent attacks or final review. Players roll one die per officer currently in the associated Army and remove each officer rolling six, then report the number removed using touch increase/decrease controls (default zero). Zero must be explicitly submitted, including when no officers are present. Record region, associated Presidency/Army and removed count in the action history, with the turn on the containing entry and a plain result in the readable report. Do not record player identities, remaining officer totals, deaths or narrative consequences. Multiple lost regions of one Army have separate results using the remaining physical pieces. Reported routs are resumable physical progress even for manual event tests; JSON saves and Undo retain the results. Legacy histories without rout data remain readable and are not backfilled. Successful defences and Indian-only battles do not request rout results.

The India map statistics always show Regions lost this turn and the Standing penalty for the next lost region. Derive the count from confirmed current-turn regionLosses history, including losses during Parliament. Count multiple losses of the same region individually, retain the count after recapture, and update it with Undo/import/load; beginning a new turn naturally resets it. Do not infer a live Standing value.

Envoy to the Mughals uses progressive touch controls rather than enumerating every legal position: choose Inside a region or On a border, then choose a region or a starting region followed by a destination. Inside placement is disabled with an explanation when no Company region exists. Only legal starts and destinations are offered. Changing mode clears the region choices; changing the start clears the destination. Selection is ephemeral, with no state changes before the existing review, Elephant movement page and final confirmation. Preserve card timing, cancellation responsibility, legalElephants rules and the highest-open-order payment.

## Elephant
March normally uses the exposed region, with Imperial Ambitions using the victorious capital after successful invasion. Company regions place it inside; subjects face their sovereign; sovereigns use the drawn front’s shape and skip their own subjects clockwise. Fully surrounded capitals use the redirect-arrow symbol and face inward from the indicated subject. Missing tile information is requested when needed. Successful conquest, Leader and foreign-invasion exceptions follow their printed conditions.

Shape directions were read from the supplied board PDF. Circle/triangle/square: Punjab Bombay/Bombay/Delhi; Delhi Maratha/Bengal/Punjab; Bengal Maratha/Delhi/Delhi; Bombay Maratha/Punjab/Hyderabad; Maratha Bombay/Bengal/Delhi; Hyderabad Madras/Maratha/Bombay; Mysore Bombay/Hyderabad/Madras; Madras Hyderabad/Mysore/Mysore. These are directional, not mirrored. A subject facing a distant capital is drawn on its boundary facing toward that capital, while its actual rebellion target remains the sovereign region.

## Foreign invasion and Parliament
Confirming a Foreign Invasion automatically generates a fresh storm die face in the app and saves it before animation. Reopening uses that saved result. West targets Bombay, South Madras, East Bengal, All targets all three in that order. Ordinary None targets the exposed region; failed War Against France with None causes no invasion. Each target’s fair d6 is generated once by the app and saved immediately in the saved action progress. Later targets use the board after earlier consequences. Successful conquest sets strength to floor(original die / 2), excluding unrest and Sepoy effects. Region Loss and foreign aftermath share one order-closure operation to avoid duplicate Cascades.

Parliament uses one view with Laws and Dilemmas boxes. The applicable laws are Royal Protection, Governor General, Envoy to China, Zamindar Taxes, Treasure Reform and Sepoy Recruitment; exclude already-active laws. Selecting a law shows only Passed in that same view; clicking it immediately records the law and displays its physical instructions without another review dialog. Unpassed laws require no entry. Only War Against France and Relief Demanded for Indian Famine appear as dilemmas, with Passed and Failed options in the same view. Dilemma Passed/Failed buttons select an outcome without applying effects or rolling dice. A separate Confirm outcome button is required; it stays disabled until an outcome is selected. Switching cards clears the selection, and closing before confirmation forgets it. Confirmed passed outcomes and failed famine record and show instructions while retaining the Parliament view. Confirmed failed France automatically rolls a fresh fair six-sided storm die, saves its exact face before animation, and enters invasion resolution. The saved phase storm is not reused. The two None faces cause no invasion; other faces map to the printed home-region targets. This roll causes no ship checks and does not alter phase event counts. The digital event stack supplies the exposed region automatically, and the printed circle is used for March and its fully dominated capital redirect. No storm-result, region or symbol selections are shown. Each target retains its saved invasion die, defence, rout and final confirmation flow; reopening or Undo must not reroll the storm. After completion the dialog returns to Parliament. Failed famine relief resolves Turmoil in all home regions and adds one unrest per Company region. Passed France instructs removal of three non-extra ships and three officers/regiments without launching an invasion. End Parliament is always available in this view without selecting or recording a card; it records completion immediately, displays Upkeep/Refresh or final-turn instructions and lets players return to the map. Impeachment, Franchise, Old Ideas, Calico Acts and Military Oversight have no recording controls here; historical records and legacy law flags remain readable. Physical voting, drawing, recovery and reshuffling remain with the players. A relevant card recovered through Old Ideas is reported using its normal applicable card entry. Deregulation remains a separate start-of-turn special session. China creation is recorded through Special Envoy or the Envoy to China law; a vacant office remains created.

The main Company opium statistic appears only while the China office exists. It shows the icon total and potential successful China trade income at £4/icon, or £5/icon with Envoy to China. The administration context shows the same proceeds and the separate £1/icon Superintendent bonus. These are estimates based on current Company territory, not recorded China rolls or actual income. With the office closed, the global opium display is hidden. Region dossiers may still show their printed icon facts.

## Blackmail and narrative
The menu contains Envoy to the Mughals, Scandal in India and Scandal on Leadenhall Street. Players resolve cancellation and rerolls before applying a card. Diplomatic Connection and Man on the Inside have no separate app workflow.

Envoy offers only legal Elephant positions and states the highest-open-order payment. Scandals offer eligible offices and record dismissal without retirement. Scandal in India includes Presidents, extant Governors or Governor General; Leadenhall Street offers the other supported offices. Office dismissal does not alter map control or repeal Governor General. A named fictional assistant delivers a short dismissal comment; the player officeholder remains anonymous. Regional rulers, full succession, claimants, treasure stories and the character roster remain future work.

## Persistence and testing
Ordinary unconfirmed action forms and previews stay only in the open dialog and are forgotten on X, Escape or Cancel. No form draft, discard confirmation or pending-action gate is created. Only committed progress is saved separately in this browser with a fingerprint of its starting campaign: a revealed digital tile, generated invasion dice, or an already rolled/drawn result restored by Undo. Such progress resumes directly at its saved step without a separate Resume menu or Discard control; closing cannot skip a tile or reroll a result. Undo of a foreign invasion retains its input and dice for resumption. Final action records include their physical instructions and input data in JSON exports.

Sources: user-supplied rulebook pp.18–33, bridge-card fronts (blackmail 4,5,7; laws and dilemmas), supplied full-board PDF, and the user-confirmed Maratha loot and Sepoy interpretations. Browser visual/touch verification is not available in this environment; rule transitions, existing-save compatibility and generated dialog flows are checked locally.

## Phase progression and portable campaign saves

Parliament laws, Famine and War Against France require explicitly completed Events in India. Begin next turn requires completed India and Finish Parliament, and is unavailable on the scenario’s final turn. These rules are enforced in both UI controls and the gameplay resolver, including before the India phase has been started. Manual event tests remain available independently. Company failure can still end the game before India (Revenue) or after the phase; ending remains blocked during the phase. No additional officeholder lockouts are tracked: players handle the consequences of dismissals.

JSON saves, named snapshots and autosave contain optional protected action progress alongside campaign state and Undo states: exact invasion rolls, defence and attack-order answers, saved phase/stack-draw results, the current resolution stage and acknowledged physical-instruction cursor. Corresponding Undo progress is included. New progress is mirrored into autosave immediately; startup recovers it from that save if the separate browser progress entry is absent. Imports validate the campaign/progress fingerprint, tile identity, die values, stage, instruction cursor and Undo pairing before replacing current play. Legacy version-one files without progress fields remain supported. Renaming a campaign with an unfinished action preserves and rebases its progress; Undo and starting a new campaign preserve recoverable previous progress. Ordinary unconfirmed forms remain ephemeral.

The save format remains version one with additive optional progress and undoProgress fields. The 6 MB backup limit is measured as UTF-8 bytes. If the complete Undo stack makes a backup too large, the oldest Undo frames are omitted until it fits; the current campaign, full current chronicle and current committed progress are retained. The app rejects a campaign that cannot fit even without Undo rather than producing an unimportable backup.

## Chronicle browsing, readable export and save controls

Campaign record provides turn and action-category button filters, newest-first pagination in pages of 25 entries, and access to the complete retained history. Changing these controls never changes campaign state. The old silent 1,000-entry truncation is removed; up to 10,000 entries are supported within the backup-size limit. Older entries already removed by previous versions cannot be reconstructed.

Export readable chronicle is available from Campaign record and Saved games. It downloads a self-contained, printable HTML report containing the current board, tracked laws, China office state, exposed stack region and all retained chronicle entries in chronological turn order. The report always includes the whole chronicle regardless of current UI filters. It escapes user-provided text and never previews unrevealed event fronts. JSON remains the format for resuming a campaign; readable reports identify unresolved actions without claiming their board effects are confirmed.

Loading, importing, deleting snapshots and starting a new campaign use touch-friendly in-app confirmations, with Cancel leaving current play unchanged. No native browser confirmation popups are required. Buttons and disclosure summaries have minimum 44 px touch targets; chronicle filters and navigation wrap on smaller screens. Automated integration tests cover recovery, snapshots, imports, exports, renaming, Undo, phase gates and these controls with native confirmations disabled. These are DOM interaction checks; actual browser rendering and physical-device touch verification remain unverified because browser preview tooling is unavailable.

## Events in India phase (implemented)

The Events in India button starts the phase, with a last-chance reminder for Envoy to the Mughals. Players choose an app roll or a physical roll. For a physical roll, five touch buttons report the distinct faces (both None faces share one button), and a separate confirmation starts the phase without generating random numbers. For an app roll, the six-faced storm die rolls once. Both paths immediately save the confirmed result in campaign state. Exact faces: East/2, West/2, South/3, All/1, None/4, None/4. Duplicate None faces preserve the correct probability. This phase roll is separate from Foreign Invasion targeting rolls, which are automatic in the app, including manual event tests. Invasion storm rolls do not cause ship checks or change the phase event count.

For affected seas, show physical ship instructions and require acknowledgement before allowing the first event. Roll once per eligible ship, excluding Company and Extra ships. China-office ships count in the East Indian Ocean. Rolls 1–2 have no effect; 3–4 fatigue a fresh ship or sink an already fatigued one; 5–6 sink. Return sunk ships to shipyards non-fatigued. Individual ship inventories and rolls remain on the table. No-storm results skip the ship step.

A persistent phase banner shows the saved storm result and completed/required count. Within the India map tab, an exposed-region panel is visible during all phases, including Company Operations. The exposed-region panel, phase progress banner and gameplay action toolbar belong to the India map page and are hidden when navigating to another tab. Draw next event reserves and saves one digital tile, reveals its front and saves the pending resolution progress. The app reveals one tile from its digital stack and supplies its front and the newly exposed back region. Previewing, pausing and entering defence information do not advance the saved event counter. Confirmation atomically applies the event and advances the counter once, then shows the exposed stack-region page before returning to the map. Shuffle and Foreign Invasion each consume one event regardless of their internal steps or number of targets. No further draws are possible after the exact quota. Finish phase explicitly completes Events in India and allows Parliament.

Blackmail cards remain available between events. Envoy to the Mughals is disabled and mechanically rejected once Events in India begins, including after the phase has completed that turn. The two scandal cards are legal after Revenue and remain available between events. Cancellation and other cards continue to be handled on the table. Revealed unresolved events must be finished before another action can replace them. Unconfirmed ordinary forms do not block other actions after closing.

Company Operations actions and Deploy are unavailable after the phase begins. Parliament and the next turn are unavailable while the phase is active. Begin next turn clears the phase marker. Phase state and progress are included in save/export/undo. Undo of phase start preserves the saved face as a resumable action rather than silently offering another roll. Older saves without a phase marker remain readable.

Sources: rulebook p.28 (storm procedure and event count), p.25 (China ships), and blackmail card 7 plus cards 4–5 (timing).


## Real event stack and manual tests

Twenty unique tile IDs preserve the exact front/back pairings supplied by the user on 15 October, with recovered modifier and symbol facts from their reference catalogue. Counts: 6 Crisis, 4 Leader, 4 Turmoil, 2 Windfall, 2 Peace, 1 Shuffle and 1 Foreign Invasion. Crisis modifiers: Delhi 0/triangle, Punjab −1/circle, Maratha +3/circle, Bombay +1/square, Bengal +1/triangle, Mysore +2/square. Leaders: Punjab +3/circle, Bombay +2/square, Hyderabad +4/triangle, Bengal +2/triangle. Peace: Mysore/square and Madras/triangle. Shuffle: Madras/circle. Foreign Invasion: Maratha/circle. Turmoil and Windfall have no movement symbol stored because neither triggers March. The reference code architecture is not reused.

The region is on each tile’s back. The symbol for March is on the drawn event front/redirect arrow, not the next back. Rulebook p.30’s Crisis/Mysore diagram confirms this distinction. Automatic event inputs derive from the reserved tile and current stack; callers cannot override them.

A fresh stack is shuffled once using Fisher–Yates and unbiased cryptographic random indexes. It persists across turns, reloads, snapshots and exports. Existing pre-stack saves receive a fresh full stack once; previously manually reported physical draws cannot be reconstructed. Old undo frames share that initial stack baseline rather than reshuffling on undo. New campaigns get fresh stacks.

State keeps draw IDs, discard IDs and one optional reserved/revealed tile. The exposed-region panel reads only the next back; it never previews the future front. Drawing commits the reservation before resolution. Closing or resuming its resolution cannot skip or redraw the reserved tile. Final event confirmation discards the tile and increments the phase counter once. Other game actions cannot replace an unresolved stack event.

Shuffle saves its two independent random permutations at draw time. With a nonempty draw pile, March uses the pre-shuffle exposed region, then the current tile is shuffled into the remainder and separately shuffled discards are placed above it. With an empty draw pile, rebuild first and March using the newly exposed region. The Shuffle tile never remains in discards, and a properly formed stack cannot run out on a different tile. Validation requires all 20 IDs exactly once across draw/discard/reserved zones.

Manual event resolution · test is in Game actions. It reports the event and region explicitly, applies the existing rules resolver and labels the history entry as a test. It leaves the digital stack and phase count untouched, including outside the phase or after its completion. Tests are blocked while a real stack tile awaits resolution. Undo reverses test map effects.

## Parliament completion and upkeep handoff

Parliament has a Finish Parliament button after Events in India completes. It works whether or not a relevant law/dilemma was recorded. Completion is saved per turn, blocks further parliamentary outcomes unless undone, and displays Upkeep and Refresh with a Begin next turn button. Complete physical upkeep/refresh before advancing. Regional control, orders, towers, unrest, Elephant and the saved event stack carry forward. On the final turn, show prize-upkeep/Final Scoring instructions and skip refresh rather than offering a seventh turn. Old saves without the Parliament marker remain supported.

## Turn guide

The left menu opens a read-only Turn guide covering all nine base phases, with scenario setup and Deregulation reminders. Touch-friendly phase buttons, sidebar shortcuts and previous/next controls provide quick access to each reminder. Each phase includes its sequence, key rules, printed rulebook page references and instructions for using the companion versus handling pieces on the table. Company Operation includes success-check results and deployment/administration reminders. The guide flags the first-turn London Season skip and the final-turn refresh exception. Reading or switching reminders does not save, advance a phase, consume randomness or change campaign history. Passed laws and card-specific exceptions take precedence over these summaries. Upkeep and Refresh remains a reference and physical handoff, not a new interactive app phase.

## End game and close the chronicle

End game is available in the main action bar and Game actions before Events in India begins and after the phase is explicitly finished. It is disabled throughout storm resolution and event resolution, including between tiles and after the last tile until Finish phase. A Company failure in Revenue goes immediately to Final Scoring; a failure during India must finish all required events first (rulebook pp.27 and 29). Parliament failure can be reported after resolving the vote. Standing is reported from the physical board, not tracked numerically by the app.

The custom closing dialog asks for Company failure, or Final turn completed when Parliament is finished on the scenario’s final turn, and an optional 2,000-character closing note. Review precedes confirmation. The saved ending records the reason, turn, note and timestamp, adds a final chronicle entry with remaining Company territory and this turn’s region-loss count, and provides physical scoring instructions. Normal endings remind players of final prize upkeep and skipping refresh; failure endings remind players of the Company failure card. Player identities, scores and winners remain at the table.

Closing preserves the final map and digital stack. A completed-chronicle banner links to Campaign record; map inspection, guide, snapshots, export and campaign renaming remain available. All gameplay transitions and deployment are blocked after closure. Undo restores the preceding open game. Export/import and snapshots preserve the ending. Older saves without the optional gameEnd field continue to load as open campaigns.

## Closing unconfirmed dialogs

X or Cancel closes Deploy immediately and forgets its Army/target choices, forces, table-roll reports, and unconfirmed preview. Ordinary actions (Tax, Add unrest, Envoy, laws, blackmail and End game) also leave no saved form entries before confirmation. Choosing a form option or previewing a calculated outcome does not count as an applied game action. The map, chronicle and phase counters change only when the player confirms the action, except for immediately committed phase starts and digital stack draws.

Revealing a digital event tile or generating an invasion die is already a game consequence, so that action’s resolution stays saved and cannot be discarded. Closing lets players inspect the map; reopening goes directly back to the saved step. Storm rolls and Shuffle permutations remain saved by their existing phase/stack mechanisms. The old draft storage key is reused only for protected progress, so upgrading clears legacy ordinary form drafts while preserving recorded dice and unresolved event resolution. Legacy deployment drafts are ignored and removed when Deploy opens. Players remain responsible for reversing any unconfirmed physical changes when they abandon a preview.

## Animated app dice

The app animates the initial Events in India storm die when rolled in the app, each automatic Foreign Invasion or War Against France targeting storm die, and every generated invasion-strength d6. Reporting a physical phase storm roll does not show an app-roll animation. Rolls requested from players on the physical table remain physical. The outcome is generated and saved before opening the animation; the animation never samples randomness or changes probabilities. Double taps cannot generate a second roll. Closing during animation leaves the saved phase or invasion result available to resume without rerolling. After about 1.1 seconds the die settles on that exact face with its readable result and Continue. Skip animation reveals it immediately; reduced-motion preferences bypass the tumble altogether. Stale animation timers cannot replace or update a later dialog, and Continue runs only once.

Storm artwork is extracted directly from page 4 of the uploaded John Company Wood Manifest.pdf: East/2 and one storm, West/2 and one storm, South/3 and one storm, All/1 and three storms, and two plain 4 faces. The cube follows the shown net; both 4 faces share one image but remain distinct equiprobable die faces. No icons or numerals are fabricated. Regular dice follow the same page’s specified red/black marbled finish with white pips (the gold-pip sample photo is explicitly overridden by its written specification). Their standard pip faces use SVG and the marbled appearance is a CSS approximation. Assets and PDF crop coordinates are documented in assets/dice/README.md.

## Dedicated Elephant and stack-region pages

Every actual Elephant position change is recorded as structured before/after positions with its physical-instruction index. Events, blackmail and successful deployment use this same information. Movement instructions are shown on dedicated pages with an exact border/facing or wholly-inside description, the previous position and a miniature vector map. No character lines, portraits or invented ruler identities are added.

Instructions before a move are acknowledged first; the movement receives its own Continue page at the correct place in the sequence. Multiple movements in an action each receive a page. A movement reached before a later defence/attack-order/invasion-roll prompt is displayed before that prompt, rather than collected after all attacks. The final review lists the remaining instructions without repeating acknowledged moves. The action still applies atomically only on final confirmation. Unconfirmed deployment remains ephemeral on X/Cancel. A pending committed event or saved roll retains its acknowledged instruction cursor in the local resolution progress, so reopening resumes without repeating acknowledged movement pages. History retains the full instructions and movement records.

After confirming a real digital stack event, show Region on top of the event stack with the resulting exposed region, control, tower strength, unrest, open/closed orders and a miniature map. Read this from the committed resulting stack, including after Shuffle; do not reuse the pre-Shuffle region used for March. Never reveal the next event front. Return to map dismisses the page without consuming another tile or advancing a phase. Closing it with X is also safe because the event has already been recorded. Manual event tests and actions that leave the stack unchanged do not produce a new-stack recap. The existing main-screen exposed-region display remains visible. Narration is deferred until gameplay functionality is settled.

## Governor actions menu

For regional Governors, the Company region dossier shows one Governor actions button. It opens two touch choices: Tax and Unsuccessful Administer. Tax reuses the automatic first/later Tax calculation. Unsuccessful Administer fixes the reason to failure and applies one unrest, or two with Zamindar Taxes; there is no second reason selector. Both routes preview and require confirmation. Opening, selecting and closing the menu make no board change and create no saved draft. The global Game actions menu uses the same grouping and asks for the region within the selected form. Phase restrictions still apply. Under Governor General, regional Governor actions are replaced by the existing Governor General Tax button; company-wide Govern/sixes controls remain separate.

## Official errata

Deployment cannot target another Presidency’s home region or a Company-controlled region assigned to another Presidency, even if an army’s own Company region borders it. The shared eligibility function supplies the restriction to global target selection and regional army buttons; deployment validation also rejects a stale or imported request for that target. Interventions in a region assigned to the acting army remain allowed when unrest or closed orders give them an effect. Tests cover all three army/Presidency pairings.

The Turn guide includes the official no-possible-family-action exception (take no action and return the opportunity token to supply), the requirement to recover a needed family piece from a prize when supply is empty with the corresponding VP loss (including firm share creation), and the complete empty-Court Chairman fallback, including the possibility of no Chairman. The attached public errata snapshot is the reference for these changes.

## Scenarios

Saved games → New game provides four touch-button choices and physical setup reminders before Start. 1710 starts on printed turn 1 and ends after 5; 1758 starts on 3 and ends after 7; 1813 starts on 5 and ends after 8; Long 1710 runs 1–8. Setup uses the supplied scenario card backs and the printed board turn track. New 1710 games also correct Hyderabad’s initially closed order. Starting state applies all towers, empire flags, closed orders, Company presidencies, spent starting-Company loot, Elephant position, laws and China-office status. Each new game shuffles a fresh event stack. No loot is awarded for Company territories already controlled at setup.

1758 starts with Bengal controlled by its Presidency and Calico Acts active. 1813 starts with all three home regions controlled by their own Presidencies, Governor General and China active, plus Calico Acts, Military Oversight and Deregulation. Long 1710 shares the standard starting map and Royal Protection. Starting regiments, ships, player cards, treasuries, Standing, Debt and share-value overlays appear as table instructions. These do not become tracked inventories.

1758 and Long 1710 provide a special Deregulation vote in Game actions before Events in India. Instructions identify its actual timing before London Season and the lined/starred Standing/Debt conditions, which players check physically. Passing records Deregulation and gives the printed debt/Standing instructions; failing gives the share-value instruction. Governor General remains independent. Ordinary Parliament cannot activate Deregulation. The Turn guide includes scenario setup and active-law reminders, including Firms between Family and Hiring and firm trade during Presidency operations. Firms’ accounts, strategies and filled orders remain on the table.

All final-turn guards, Parliament handoff instructions, saved filenames, headers and chronicle reports use the selected scenario. Existing saves retain their map and history; optional newly tracked laws may be absent in older saves. Legacy 1710 saves already on turn 6 remain readable and can finish, but cannot advance. New game remains reversible with Undo, including restoration of an older pending event or saved die result.

## Map readability

Region names are centered at hand-tuned label anchors independent of Elephant and order geometry. Tower levels use small stacked tier symbols and unrest uses red cube symbols, both with exact numeric counts including zero. At most three pieces are drawn per symbol to keep high imported counts bounded; the number remains authoritative. These are vector representations, not component scans.

Company territories have a red Company plaque naming their presidency and a red dashed boundary. Empire capitals have a crown and Empire Capital plaque, with a heavier solid boundary. Their vassals explicitly say Vassal and name the same empire; both share a capital-specific accent color. Original regional fills remain unchanged. Selected regions still draw last and have a solid dark selection outline. All status markers update directly from the current board state, have accessible text and do not intercept map touches. The map legend explains the symbols.


## Rules Library audit — 22 October 2026

Authority: Buried Giant Studios Rules Library, John Company, English, displayed as 4th Printing (Work in Progress). See `docs/buried-giant-rules-audit.md` for the comparison and limits. Explicit corrections supplement the supplied PDF and earlier official errata; omissions from the WIP transcription do not repeal printed rules.

Foreign Invasion and failed War Against France resolve every primary target, including defence, officer routs, losses, foreign aftermath and required Elephant redirects, before one set of additional unrest rebellions. Additional rebellions trigger only if at least one primary target was Company-controlled. Eligibility is evaluated after all primary outcomes; defended primaries have cleared unrest and lost primaries are Indian-controlled. Use Presidency order and current, exhausted Army availability. A later primary must not be displaced by a premature secondary rebellion. The new tower remains floor(raw invasion die / 2), without unrest or Sepoy additions. Each order-closure effect is applied once.

The Turn guide now states that timing explicitly and retains opportunity-marker placement when forming a firm. End-game instructions explicitly state the winner and tiebreak procedure. These reminders do not track player scores or firms.
